title: Evaluating the Semantic Specificity of Representation Steering in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.29431v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Localized Representation Steering (LRS) is widely used to correct reasoning pathologies in large language models. However, standard benchmark evaluations can easily be fooled by superficial label overrides, creating a false impression of reasoning circuit repairs. In this work, we propose Cross-Rule Transfer (CRT), a diagnostic framework that audits representational interventions by evaluating them on rule families where the model is natively competent. Evaluating late-layer LRS for a widespread logical failure, contradiction blindness, reveals that the intervention merely injects a global label bias: applying the steering vector to rules the model already handles correctly (99.6% baseline) degrades performance to 40.4% by forcing false contradiction predictions. We support this diagnosis with four complementary controls (direct logit bias equivalence, control vector label-flipping, cross-model grafting, and early-layer steering checks),

translated_title: 评估语言模型中表征引导的语义特异性
translated_abstract: 局部化表征引导被广泛用于纠正大语言模型中的推理病态。然而，标准基准评估很容易被表面的标签覆盖所欺骗，从而造成推理电路已被修复的假象。在这项工作中，我们提出了跨规则迁移，这是一个诊断框架，通过在模型本身已具备能力的规则族上评估表征干预来对其进行审计。针对一种普遍存在的逻辑失效——矛盾盲视——对后层LRS的评估表明，该干预仅仅是注入了一个全局标签偏置：将引导向量应用于模型原本已能正确处理的规则（99.6%基线）时，性能会因被迫产生错误的矛盾预测而下降至40.4%。我们通过四种互补的对照实验支持这一诊断（直接logit偏置等价性、对照向量标签翻转、跨模型移植以及早期层引导检查），
tldr: 该论文提出跨规则迁移（CRT）诊断框架，揭示后层表征引导并非真正修复推理电路，而只是注入全局标签偏置，导致模型在原本已正确处理的规则上性能从99.6%骤降至40.4%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Cross-Rule Transfer (CRT), a diagnostic framework revealing that late-layer representation steering merely injects a global label bias rather than repairing reasoning circuits, degrading performance on rules the model already masters from 99.6% to 40.4%.
